*** Begin Patch

+# Workflow and Tooling Issues to Fix
+
+There are several problems with how we use tickets and specs, and with how our agents use those tools.
+
+- In many sessions, especially with smaller sub-agents, I see failed tool calls caused by small issues. This seems related in part to the MCP cost gate, which is still too strict about how the model has to be passed into a call.
+- Many problems do not even raise errors. For example, some agents seem to think they can update a ticket description while preserving the previous content, but the update actually overwrites it and the ticket content is lost.
+- Specs have a similar problem: it is currently possible to send an update with empty content. In complex workflows, that forces extra verification just to confirm whether anything was updated. Empty spec updates should be rejected so agents can trust that a successful call really changed something.
+- Handoffs also need a persistent workflow step list or step graph that encodes the next steps. That is the most important part of a handoff, and it is missing right now. At minimum, the handoff should contain the next steps. Ideally, it should contain a complete graph so the next session can continue from a real plan instead of starting over.
+- In the agent instructions, multiple orchestrated agents created the same tickets in sequence. The top-level orchestrator first had a ticket track created, then reviewed it, and then a new sub-agent duplicated many of the tickets one-to-one. This suggests agents are not checking what already exists before acting.
+- The default behavior should be to treat every requested change as a delta from the current state. A new entity should only be created when it is truly necessary, whether that entity is a ticket, a spec, or something else.
+- We also need instructions and possibly a separate prompt template for recovery after an interruption. When a session is interrupted, the next agent should find the loose ends and resume at the right point instead of assuming the interrupted part is already complete or restarting at a rough boundary.
+- Finally, we need an explicit Research Agent for online search.
+
+Open questions:
+
+- The exact intended handling of the MCP cost gate is unclear from the transcript; the current request is to make tool calls less fragile and less strictly blocked by model-passing requirements.
*** End Patch
